beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Scope and Faculty Pilot Framework as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. This course examines current topics in Languages and Tools. Consider this worked case: A department head proposes a new undergraduate offering focused on compiler design. On screen, display a flowchart showing faculty proposal -> pilot course -> cluster classification (Languages and Tools or Security). List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Course Scope and Faculty Pilot Framework
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a flowchart showing faculty proposal -> pilot course -> cluster classification (Languages and Tools or Security).

beats.narration: Now define Cluster Classification System precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to the Languages and Tools cluster, the Security cluster, or both clusters. Consider this worked case: A proposed seminar on memory safety analysis is classified under both clusters. On screen, show a Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labeled 'Languages and Tools' and 'Security', with a course title in the intersection. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
beats.title: Cluster Classification System
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labeled 'Languages and Tools' and 'Security', with a course title in the intersection.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Language Reference Structure operates in a concrete sequence. The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics. Consider this worked case: A reference document outlines how Python handles variable binding and exception propagation. On screen, list the specified reference components in a hierarchical outline format. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Language Reference Structure
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | List the specified reference components in a hierarchical outline format.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Object Model and Namespaces and make the decision criteria explicit. Names are bound to objects within namespaces and scopes. Consider this worked case: A function call binds the parameter name to a specific object instance in the local scope. On screen, illustrate a namespace tree with nested scopes and object references pointing to shared memory addresses. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Object Model and Namespaces
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a namespace tree with nested scopes and object references pointing to shared memory addresses.

beats.narration: Apply Control Flow and Exceptions to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate. Consider this worked case: A division by zero triggers an exception that jumps to a try-except block. On screen, draw a control flow graph with a normal path and an exception path branching to a handler node. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Control Flow and Exceptions
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Draw a control flow graph with a normal path and an exception path branching to a handler node.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in LLVM Intermediate Representation, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow. Consider this worked case: A compiler translates a high-level loop into a sequence of LLVM IR basic blocks with phi nodes. On screen, render a simplified LLVM IR module showing a function, basic blocks, and a phi instruction at a merge point. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
beats.title: LLVM Intermediate Representation
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Render a simplified LLVM IR module showing a function, basic blocks, and a phi instruction at a merge point.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Phi Instructions and Control Flow with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge. Consider this worked case: A phi node chooses between two loop iteration values based on whether the loop condition was true or false. On screen, show a control flow graph with two incoming edges to a block containing a phi instruction that selects between two values. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Phi Instructions and Control Flow
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a control flow graph with two incoming edges to a block containing a phi instruction that selects between two values.

beats.narration: Use Memory Operations and Verification to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Load and store instructions make memory access explicit. Consider this worked case: The verifier rejects an IR module where a store instruction targets an untyped memory location. On screen, display a before-and-after comparison of invalid IR (with a type mismatch) and valid IR (with explicit memory types). Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Memory Operations and Verification
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a before-and-after comparison of invalid IR (with a type mismatch) and valid IR (with explicit memory types).

beats.narration: Connect Compiler Phase Separation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation. Consider this worked case: A frontend parser generates ASTs, while a backend optimizer restructures the IR for a specific CPU architecture. On screen, present a linear pipeline diagram with distinct stages: Parsing -> Semantic Analysis -> Lowering -> Verification -> Optimization -> Code Generation. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Compiler Phase Separation
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a linear pipeline diagram with distinct stages: Parsing -> Semantic Analysis -> Lowering -> Verification -> Optimization -> Code Generation.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Consider this worked case: A review checklist verifies that the proposed course includes defined learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs. On screen, show a checklist template with checkboxes for prerequisites, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a checklist template with checkboxes for prerequisites, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs.

sources.excerpt: The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics. Python objects have identity, a type, and a value. Names are bound to objects within namespaces and scopes. Expressions produce values, while statements control execution and bindings. Exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate. The import system searches for modules and binds loaded modules into a namespace. Programs should be reasoned about through explicit state, control flow, data representation, contracts, tests, and observable behavior. sources.author: LLVM Project
sources.excerpt: LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow. A module contains global values, functions, declarations, and metadata. A function contains basic blocks, and every basic block ends with a terminator instruction. Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge. Load and store instructions make memory access explicit. Valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules. The verifier reports IR that violates those rules. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.
